summary: Full end-to-end testing of CloudCollab collaborative workspace platform completed. All 36 backend pytest tests pass. All 14 frontend UI flows verified (auth, workspaces, documents CRUD, file upload/delete, projects, Kanban tasks with status change, member invite/remove, protected/public route redirects). Fixed 1 critical backend bug (jwt.JWTError -> jwt.InvalidTokenError) that returned 500 on any invalid JWT.

critical_code_review_comments: FIXED: server.py get_current_user used jwt.JWTError which does not exist in PyJWT - caused 500 on malformed tokens. Replaced with jwt.InvalidTokenError.
JWT_SECRET_KEY default is a placeholder in backend/.env - ensure production deployment uses a strong secret.
CORS_ORIGINS is '*' with allow_credentials=True - browsers will reject credentialed requests; consider setting explicit origin(s).
File uploads: server does not enforce max file size / type validation. Consider adding safety limits.
server.py is ~950 lines. Recommend splitting into modules (auth, workspaces, documents, files, projects, tasks) for maintainability.
test_credentials: None persisted (each test run registers fresh users with timestamped emails to avoid conflicts). Example format: test-{tag}-{ts}@example.com / TestPass123!
seed_data_creation: No seed data required; tests self-provision users/workspaces/documents/files/projects/tasks and clean up via delete endpoints where applicable.
context_for_next_testing_agent: pytest.ini enforces `-n 2 --dist loadscope` (pytest-xdist). Tests are structured with class-scoped fixtures so each class is self-contained across workers - do NOT rely on cross-class shared state. Backend URL: REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. All frontend interactive elements use data-testid from /app/frontend/src/constants/testIds/. File upload input is `input#file-upload` (hidden). Task status select is Radix combobox inside task card (button[role='combobox']).
rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: any request with a malformed JWT returned 500. RCA: backend used `jwt.JWTError` which is defined in python-jose but NOT in PyJWT (the installed library, per requirements.txt uses `pyjwt`). The bare `AttributeError: module 'jwt' has no attribute 'JWTError'` bubbled out of the exception handler and produced HTTP 500. Mitigation: replaced with `jwt.InvalidTokenError` which is the correct base exception in PyJWT and covers InvalidSignatureError, DecodeError, etc. Verified via new test `TestAuth::test_auth_me_bad_token` which now passes with 401.
